Comments: On 11/15/2024, an complaint inspection was conducted at the SHARPNACK Well site in Cumberland Township, Greene County in response to a anonymous complaint reported to the department on 11/14/2024.The following was observed during inspection:-Act 9 sign present at site entrance (Photo 1)-It appears sediment and gravel washed onto township road-Kurans Road due to accelerated erosion rills on access road and well site entrance (Photo 2-8).-I observed deep erosion rills along both sides of the access road. Comments: The operator contacted the Department on Monday, September 16 to report a spill that was found at the Warrant 5573 W87 well site. This site was previously impacted by a 10+ barrel spill that occurred 8/4/16 (ID #2509096). The operator at the time, SWEPI LP, has since sold the well to Pennhills Resources, who is currently operating the well. SWEPI LP is remediating the site under the Department's Oil and Gas Spill Policy. Present on site for this inspection were DEP ECB representative Barry Stanton, Pennhills Resources' Stuart and Tom Morris, and SWEPI LP's Pat Bernethy, and myself. An unknown, but likely small, volume of oil leaked from a line at the site and leached down through rock and into a seep on the hillside below. A small amount of oil was visible in two siphon dams constructed as containment just below the site, as well as in a channel leading to a previously constructed siphon dam. A small amount of this oil was found leaking into an UNT of a Chappel Fork that was previously impacted. The total length of impact from the spill site is approximately 400 horizontal feet. The operator has dug up the line to determine where the leak occurred, and is collecting oil on absorbent pads. Discussion was made regarding the responsibility of each party regarding remediation and reporting. Further inspection will be done on this site as necessary.

Report Details
Operator Alpha Shale Res Lp

Violation Code 78.73(a) - GENERAL PROVISION FOR WELL CONSTRUCTION AND OPERATION - Operator failed to construct and operate the well in accordance with 25 Pa. Code Chapter 78 and ensure that the integrity of the well is maintained and health, safety, environment and property are protected.
Violation ID 754355
Permit API 059-25981
Unconventional Y
County Greene
Municipality Jackson Twp
Inspection Type Routine/Complete Inspection
Inspection Date 2016-03-08
Comments The Department conducted an inspection of the Alpha Unit 2 8H on March 8, 2016. The well is properly identified and is equipped for production. The Department completed a review of the 8H well record. The Department has determined after review of the 8H well record, that the surface casing (20-inch) set depth does not meet the regulations specified in 25 Pa. Code § 78.83(c). The well record formation report details that three freshwater zones were identified on the pad. According to the well record freshwater was encounter at 38ft, 115ft, and 130ft (drillers log). The 24-inch borehole was drilled to 188ft and the 20-inch casing was set at 168ft and cemented. The completed 20-inch surface casing set depth is only 38ft below the deepest identified freshwater zone, instead of the required minimum of 50ft as specified by 25 Pa. Code § 78.83(c).

Violations for this release have been cited against well permit number 117-21999 and are considered immediately corrected.

Comments: On March 2, 2026, the Department conducted an inspection in response to a spill at the Marchezak John well pad in Somerset Township, Washington County. Accompanying the Department during this inspection are Range Resources representatives Denny Furmanek and Kevin Rudd. According to the spill report, approximately 25 gallons of diesel fuel were released to the surface of the well pad on February 28, 2026, at 9:30 PM.Prior to starting this inspection, the Department spoke via phone with Range Resources representative Derek Zofchak, who explained that the release occurred when a fuel truck experienced a fuel line failure while filling an on-site storage tank. Zofchak reported that remediation was completed on the day the release occurred, and that impacted material was placed in a rolloff dumpster on site.An Erosion and Sedimentation Control General Permit (ESCGP) for this site was terminated on 11/20/2017.The following was observed during the inspection:The Act 9 sign is installed at the entrance of the access road and is not obscured from view by vegetation, in accordance with 78a.55 (photo 1). The Emergency Response Plan (ERP), Preparedness Prevention and Contingency (PPC) plan, Containment plan, and Safety Data Sheets (SDS) are on site in the mailbox (photos 3-6). The ERP and PPC plan appear to contain the sections required by 78a.55. Setup of on-site secondary containment is not yet complete. However, Furmanek had the Containment inspection log available during this inspection (photo 15). The drill permits are on site in the company trailer (photo 16).The location where the 2/28/2026 diesel spill occurred appears to be freshly backfilled with stone (photo 7). No evidence of spilled diesel fuel, such as staining, odor, or a rainbow sheen was observed in this location. The fuel storage tank is placed within secondary containment (photo 8). A rolloff box is on site which reportedly contains the impacted material (photo 13). Rudd and Furmanek explained that air drilling operations have been completed. Drilling operations are expected to continue on the day of this inspection (photo 14). Four gas wells are planned to be drilled during this project. Five gas wells are on site that appear to be equipped for production. The GPU units and Dehy unit are not equipped with secondary containment (photos 9 and 10). However, the producing wells on site were drilled prior to the promulgation of 78a. The production tanks and the surrounding secondary containment do not have any observable fluid leaks (photo 12). All other storage containers and machinery on site that appear to contain regulated substances are placed within secondary containment (photo 11). The secondary containments on site appear to be in good condition at the time of inspection, with no observable holes or tears.The access road and well pad appear to be stable at the time of inspection with no concerns relating to accelerated erosion and sedimentation (photos 2 and 14). Furmanek explained that the well pad was expanded adjacent to the production tanks to better accommodate vehicle traffic for drilling and stimulation operation (photo 13). This location will be assessed in a future inspection, as further review is needed.Based on observations from this inspection, violations shall be noted and immediately corrected against the 2/28/2026 diesel fuel release.Transmittal of this inspection report was delayed due to an IT Error.

Unconventional: Yes

Inspection Date: 2019-03-21
Comments: Inspection conducted in response to the report of a release of produced water that impacted the pad surface the night before at approximately 1800 and discovered around 1900. It was originally reported by a Rockdale contractor, First Priority Safety Consulting, that an estimated ten gallons had been released from a valve on the on-site AST to containment. The consultant reported that the containment had overflowed and approximately five gallons reached the pad surface. During the inspection, three wells were staged for flowback. Also during the inspection, a roll-off box was removed from the area next to the AST where the spill was reported to have occurred. A puddle in the area of the AST had a conductivity of 5.2 mS/cm. Before departing the site, I called Tony Ronquillo, water supervisor for Rockdale, and left a voicemail letting him know that i had found a high conductivity puddle. Later that day, Tony called me back and said that a Rockdale representative would come out to the site to do additional conductivity screening and he would have a vac truck out to suck up the puddle. Violations noted and considered immediately corrected.

properties.content:
Report Details
Inspection Client: PENNHILLS RESOURCES LLC
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 4/17/2023
Violation Code: 78.57(a) - CONTROL, STORAGE AND DISPOSAL OF PRODUCTION FLUIDS - Operator failed to collect the brine and other fluids produced during operation, service and plugging of the well in a tank, pit or a series of pits or tanks, or other device approved by the Department or Operator discharged brine or other fluids on or into the ground or into waters of the Commonwealth.
Violation ID: 991890
Permit API: 053-27474
Unconventional: No
County: Forest
Municipality: Howe Twp
Inspection Type: Routine/Complete Inspection
Inspection Date: 4/17/2023
Comments: This inspection was conducted in response to a third party report of crude oil accumulated outside of the tank battery located at this well site.Upon my arrival, I observed a steel stock tank within an earthen containment located behind a conventional well that is equipped with a pump jack. There are currently no appreciable accumulations evident inside of the containment. There is evidence of recent earth disturbance along the western wall of the earthen containment. Just beyond the west/southwest corner of the tank battery, aged crude oil is present over an approximate 50' path of varying widths across the forest floor. At this time, there is no active discharge and the released product appears to have remained within an isolated swale/low lying area. It appears that the source of the product originates from the vicinity of the tank battery, however with the well being in close proximity, the source of the released crude oil is currently unclear. No watercourses appear to have been impacted by this release.Stuart Morris of Pennhills was contacted after this inspection and I relayed my findings to him. Stuart was not aware of any releases from the tank battery, but he did state that the well was recently serviced. Pennhills intends to investigate the matter and begin cleanup operations.It is requested that Pennhills provide an explanation of what occurred on the well site to result in the crude oil release in their response to the Notice of Violation (NOV) that is included in this inspection report. Please note other information that is requested in the NOV.Upcoming inspections will be conducted to evaluate the status of cleanup efforts and to review or further investigate the source of the release.

Comments: This conventional well is equipped for production with a pump jack. A sign containing the API number, well name, and operator information was posted on a stake near the well. This inspection was conducted in response to a phone call from JR McLaughlin, a representative from Bull Run Resources, reporting a minor leak which had occurred at Well M22. Upon arrival to the site, it was evident that crude oil had recently leaked from a faulty line near the well head. The discharged crude oil remained on the well site. It is estimated that less than 1 barrel of crude oil has been released as part of this incident. No waterways have been affected from the event.The broken line had already been repaired before arriving to the site. Several workers from Bull Run Resources were actively shoveling contaminated soil and snow to be removed from the site. An excavator had been used to scrape the ground surface where the crude oil had discharged. The excavated area was seeded and mulched upon arrival to the site. Given there is no ongoing discharge and the impacted area appears to have been sufficiently remediated, the violations associated with this incident are considered corrected. A future inspection will be conducted to ensure that the initial remediation efforts were sufficient.

Comments: On site inspection conducted to review overall pad conditions and to inspect the two Select Energy Services 22K/26K Modular Aboveground Storage Structure (MASS) in use for well stimulation operations. Meeting on site today with Greylock Consultant Brandon Mitchell. Weather conditions at time of inspection are overcast and 24 degrees F. The site is snow and ice covered due to recent precipitation. According to Mr. Mitchell, a Halliburton frac operation is currently conducting well stimulation operations on the 1UH Utica well (API#105-21963). The crew is on stage 7 of 100 on the first well of two on site. Stimulation activity is expected to take around three more weeks. The north MASS is holding produced fluid offloaded from trucks, while the south MASS has production fluid blended with freshwater prior to transferring to tanks adjacent to the frac equipment. Each MASS is holding approximately 8,000 barrels at time of inspection. On pad fluid transfer of production fluid from trucks to the MASS Is conducted on secondary containment with rig mats (photo 2). During this inspection, the Department screened puddles broken through ice within and outside containment structures for elevated conductivity using an Oakton PCTS50 meter. No evidence of spills or produced fluid leaks are observed from the MASS's, fluid transfer lines, or pumping and valves at time of inspection.There are no new violations and no violations associated with Modular Aboveground Storage. Violations are outstanding against API #: 105-21962: 35 P.S. 691.402(b); 25 PA; 78a.57(a); 35 P.S. 6018.301. See inspection report #3878285 for additional details.

The Department requests a copy of the sample results when they become available. Violations noted.

Comments: This inspection was performed following a report from DCNR that a hunter believed that there was a possible brine discharge from this location. The email was forwarded on 11/18/22, and it had been brought to the operator's attention on 11/17.It appears as though a brine leak has occurred sometime between DEP's 4/20/22 inspection and now. It is uncertain which tank the leak is emanating from, as the containment has been compromised and deer tracks are evident throughout.Some volume of brine has leached through the soil and come out on the east side of the containment on the edge of a swale. The swale is currently running water, with slightly elevated conductivity noted in the water. Followup inspection will be done as necessary.

Comments: The Pennsylvania Department of Environmental Protection (DEP) completed an administrative inspection on Seneca Resource's Peffer Strong 483 35H on 10/5/2022. The inspection was conducted to summarize analytical sample results from samples collected on 9/6/2022 at the well site.On 7/7/2022, violations of 25 Pa. Code 78a.56(a), CSL 402(b), and SWMA 301 were cited against API #117-22110 based on analytical sample results from a sample collected on 6/23/2022 indicating the presence of a regulated substance on the pad surface, off containment. Three areas with the presence of material or water with elevated conductivity were identified in the 6/23/2022 inspection report: pooled fluid near the entrance of the pad, pad material in front of the produced water offload area and pad material located just southeast of the gas processing unit's (GPUs) containment.On 9/6/2022, the pad surface area located just southeast of the GPUs' secondary containment was retaining fluid that was field measured at ~3.72mS/cm. Sample 0983-344 was collected from the pooled fluid. The analytical sample results for this sample are attached as a file and photo (photo #2). Just east of the GPUs' containment structure, a rock-lined channel used for the conveyance of stormwater into the site's sediment traps is located at the base of the pad's cut slope. On 9/6/2022, fluid within the channel was field measured at ~2.30mS/cm and sample 0983-343 was collected for the channel. The analytical sample results for this sample are attached as a file and photo (photo #3).On 9/6/2022, the secondary containment structure surrounding the wellheads and processing equipment near the center of the pad was observed to be actively overflowing. A violation of 25 Pa. Code 78a.64a(e) regarding the failure to remove stormwater as soon as possible and prior to the capacity of secondary containment being reduced by 10% or more was cited against API #117-22110. Seneca Resource's notice of violation response is attached as a file and will be uploaded to eFACTS. Sample 0983-345 was collected from fluid with a sheen observed overtopping the containment structure. The analytical sample results for this sample are attached as a file and photo (photo #1).The DEP highly recommends conducting additional screening and potential remedial work.Violations of the following cited against API #117-22110 will remain outstanding at this time:25 Pa. Code 78a.56(a)35 P.S. 6018.30135 P.S. 691.402(b)25 Pa. Code 78a.64a(e)

Report Details
Inspection Client: DAKOTA OIL & GAS CO
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 4/28/2025
Violation Code: 91.34(A) - ACTIVITIES UTILIZING POLLUTANTS - Failure to take necessary measures to prevent the substances from directly or indirectly reaching waters of this Commonwealth, through accident, carelessness, maliciousness, hazards of weather or from another cause.
Violation ID: 8231831
Permit API: 129-26521
Unconventional: No
County: Westmoreland
Municipality: Upper Burrell Township
Inspection Type: Follow-up Inspection
Inspection Date: 4/28/2025
Comments: On April 28, 2025, an inspection was conducted at the Chabal 2 well site in Upper Burrell Township, Westmoreland County. The purpose of this inspection was to follow up to IR 3966229 where violations issued from IR 3965337 were left outstanding, as the start of remediation was postponed to the day of this inspection due to forecasted inclement weather. No impacts to the Waters of the Commonwealth were observed during the time of IR 3966229, and the impacted area was covered with plastic sheeting in preparation for the weather.The following was observed:The well head is equipped with a well tag appears to be free of fluid leaks at the time of inspection (see photos 2 and 3). The operator's information is posted on the separator (see photo 4). The body of the brine tank appears to be sound at the time of inspection (see photos 5). What appears to be a covered excavation stockpile was observed onsite, which may be from remediation work that has been conducted thus far (see photo 6). The path of brown staining that was observed traveling downslope from the brine tank during the time of IR 3965337 remains covered with plastic sheeting, and appears to have been excavated near the brine tank (see photos 7, 8, and 11). A soil conductivity reading was taken adjacent to the brine tank where it appears that impacted material was removed (see photo 9). Although the soil conductivity in this location did not appear to be elevated above that of the surrounding soil, some staining remained on the conductivity meter (see photo 10). Therefore it appears that additional excavation may be necessary in this location. Oil absorbent booms remain placed downslope of the covered impacted area (see photos 12 and 13). No evidence of visual impacts and/or elevated conductivity were detected down slope of impacted area (see photos 14 and 15).Based on observations from this inspection, it appears that remediation work has begun and the impacted area remains adequately protected to mitigate risk of the impact being spread by stormwater. However, the Department recommends that the operator assess and evaluate the excavated area adjacent to the brine tank for any additional remediation that may be needed.Violations issued from IR 3965337 shall remain outstanding.
